This pathway describes how that death-promoting fragment is restrained.

target.name: tendon development
target.description: Tendons transmit the force of muscle contraction to bone, and their development builds a tissue that must withstand repeated tension without rupturing. The programme specifies tendon progenitors from limb and axial mesenchyme and then drives their maturation into aligned, collagen-rich fibres; failure of it leaves joints unable to convert muscle shortening into movement, and weakened matrix underlies tendinopathy and tendon rupture.

target.description: Cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation is the expansion of cells already committed to a heart muscle fate but still able to divide, and it determines how much myocardium is built during development and how much regenerative reserve remains afterwards. target.name: MPS I - Hurler syndrome (HS-GAG degradation)
target.description: Heparan sulfate is dismantled inside the lysosome by an ordered series of exo-enzymes, and alpha-L-iduronidase performs one obligatory step: removal of non-reducing terminal alpha-L-iduronic acid residues. When IDUA activity is lost, the degradative chain stalls and undegraded heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate accumulate in lysosomes throughout the body, spilling into urine.
